source_note: Structural/topical citations from NAVSEA S0570-AC-CCM-010/8010, 'Industrial Ship Safety Manual for Fire Prevention and Response,' Distribution Statement A (approved for public release, distribution unlimited), dated 06 Feb 2014, smoothed version 26 Aug 2014, hosted at NAVSEA's own FOIA reading room. This is a SITE-SCOPED ruleset -- installation='PSNS' -- not a universal Navy-wide source. A different installation/command (NASNI, NAVSTA Everett, SURFPAC vs AIRPAC vs AIRLANT, etc.) may operate under different governing instructions; this file should not be treated as applicable outside the installation it's tagged for. Only HOT_WORK is covered -- this manual does not address confined_space, working_aloft, fall_protection, or over_the_side at all, so no entries exist for those categories and none should be added here (see case_data/cases_v1.json for those).

procedures.summary: Hot work requires written authorization before commencing: written notice, designated signing authority approval, posting of the notice at the work site, and notification to the Commanding Officer's representative.

procedures.section: Chapter 4.3 - Gas-Free Procedures and Special Hazards
procedures.summary: Hot work is governed by gas-free testing procedures; certain compartments/spaces are restricted from hot work; protective coverings, precautions around lines/piping carrying flammable or combustible fluids, proximity controls around flammables/combustibles, restrictions near ammunition/explosives, and special precautions for battery-charging areas all apply.

procedures.section: Chapter 4.4.3 - Limitations to Single Fire Watch with Multiple Hot Workers
procedures.summary: A single fire watch may cover multiple hot workers in one work area, subject to limitations: no more than four hot workers may be attended by a single fire watch, the fire watch must have an unobstructed view of all hot work operations from one fixed location with no physical obstructions, the fire watch cannot rove between compartments while on duty, and a means of communicating with all hot workers must be provided so the fire watch can immediately halt operations if a fire occurs.

procedures.section: Chapter 4.4.4 - Hot Work Involving Multiple Levels
procedures.summary: When hot material from hot work could involve more than one level (trunks, machinery spaces, scaffolding), a fire watch shall be stationed at each level unless positive means are in place to prevent the spread or fall of hot material.
If a hot work job involves multiple blind compartments (spaces not within a fire watch's direct line of sight), fire watches shall be posted simultaneously in each blind compartment involved.

Fire zone boundaries must be maintained and marked; temporary access cuts through fire zone boundaries during industrial work are permitted only under controlled conditions (non-combustible fume-tight closures, no aluminum) and must be recorded in an up-to-date record of boundary openings kept aboard ship; disabling or degrading a boundary closure requires FSC approval and a temporary closure system such as fire-resistant smoke curtains.

procedures.section: Chapter 11.1.7 - Boundaries on Carrier Type Ships
procedures.summary: On carrier-type ships, hangar division door travel paths must remain unobstructed so the doors can be operated in a fire; if maintenance renders a door mechanically inoperable, a means (e.g. a chain-fall) must be provided to close it, and if a door will be totally immovable, the work must be sequenced and approved by the FSC so at least one set of doors is always available to close.
